rulers.title: king of Bernicia and subject-ruler of Deira

ledger.x: c. 450: Anglian warriors found the kingdom of Deira between the Humber and the Tees. Infobox 'Established: c. 450'; the kingdom was 'probably created in the third quarter of the fifth century' after warriors invaded the Derwent valley; the first certainly recorded king, Ælla, belongs to the late sixth century. c. 604: Deira is united with Bernicia under Æthelfrith. Deira page: 'After his death [Æthelric, 589/599 to 604], Deira was subject to king Æthelfrith of Bernicia, who united the two kingdoms into Northumbria', with the infobox 'Shared crown with Bernicia: 604'. 12 October 633: Edwin is killed at Hatfield Chase and Deira goes to Osric.

wars.name: Æthelfrith's takeover of Deira
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith gained control of Deira around 604; Æthelric's reign ended and Edwin went into exile.

wars.name: Battle of the River Idle
wars.outcome: Rædwald defeated and killed Æthelfrith in 616 and 'installed Edwin as king of Northumbria'; Edwin ruled Deira and Bernicia.

wars.name: Battle of Hatfield Chase
wars.outcome: 'A decisive victory for Gwynedd and the Mercians'; Edwin was killed and Northumbria divided into Bernicia (Eanfrith) and Deira (Osric).

certainty.note: The page gives the Humber, the Tees and the western edge of the Vale of York, with Elmet beyond; no treaty or survey line.
